title: Short Messages and Personal Notes
description: Learn how to write simple A1-level personal messages, postcards, and basic form information using clear everyday French.

lessons.title: Writing a Text Message / SMS
lessons.description: Learn how to write a short casual message to invite a friend and confirm simple plans.

grammar.title: Casual Message Structure
grammar.text: A short informal French message usually begins with a friendly greeting like 'Salut', followed by a simple question or invitation. Use short sentences and finish with a casual closing such as 'À bientôt' or 'Bisous' when writing to a close friend.

lessons.reading: Salut Emma ! Ça va ? Tu veux venir au cinéma avec moi ce soir ? Le film commence à 18h. Réponds-moi vite. À bientôt ! Lucas

exercises.question: Which greeting is suitable for a casual SMS to a friend?
What is Lucas inviting Emma to do?
Salut Emma ! *** va ?
Tu veux venir au cinéma avec *** ?
Which closing is informal and friendly?

lessons.title: Writing a Holiday Postcard
lessons.description: Learn how to write a simple postcard describing the weather, location, activities, and greetings.

grammar.title: Simple Postcard Format
grammar.text: A postcard usually starts with 'Cher' or 'Chère' plus the person's name. Then write where you are, describe the weather, mention one or two activities, and finish with a short closing such as 'À bientôt' or 'Amitiés'.

lessons.reading:
Chère Léa,
Je suis à Nice avec ma famille. Il fait beau et chaud. Le matin, je vais à la plage. L'après-midi, je visite la ville. C'est très agréable.
À bientôt,
Sophie

exercises.question: Where is Sophie?
Which phrase describes good weather?
Chère *** ,
Le matin, je vais à la ***.
Which closing is appropriate for a postcard?

lessons.title: Filling Out Forms
lessons.description: Learn how to understand and complete basic French forms with personal information.

grammar.title: Capital Letters and Form Labels
grammar.text: French forms often use short labels such as 'Nom', 'Prénom', and 'Adresse'. Write names and places with capital letters. Dates in French are often written in the order day, month, year, for example: 12/04/2001.

lessons.reading:
Nom : Martin
Prénom : Clara
Date de naissance : 12/04/2001
Nationalité : française
Adresse : 15 rue Victor Hugo
Ville : Paris
Pays : France
Courriel : [clara.martin@email.com](mailto:clara.martin@email.com)

exercises.question: What does 'Prénom' mean?
Which label asks for email?
*** : Martin
In the sample form, what is Clara's city?

title: Formal and Everyday Correspondence
description: Learn how to write simple polite emails, thank-you notes, and invitations for everyday situations.

lessons.title: Writing a Polite Email
lessons.description: Learn how to write a short formal email asking for information about a class or hotel.

grammar.title: Polite Email Structure
grammar.text: A polite French email begins with 'Bonjour Madame' or 'Bonjour Monsieur'. State your request clearly with 'Je voudrais...' or 'Je cherche...'. End with 'Merci' and a polite closing such as 'Cordialement'.

lessons.reading:
Bonjour Madame,
Je voudrais des informations sur le cours de français A1. Est-ce que le cours est disponible le samedi ? Merci beaucoup.
Cordialement,
Adam Bello

exercises.question: Which opening is polite for a formal email?
What information does Adam ask for?
Je voudrais des *** sur le cours de français A1.

***,
Adam Bello
Which closing is best for a polite email?

lessons.title: Writing a Thank-You Note
lessons.description: Learn how to write a short message thanking someone for a dinner, gift, or kind action.

grammar.title: Thanking Someone Clearly
grammar.text: To thank someone in French, use 'Merci pour...' followed by the thing or action. Example: 'Merci pour le cadeau.' You can add a short positive sentence like 'C'était très gentil' or 'J'ai beaucoup aimé le dîner'.

lessons.reading:
Chère Marie,
Merci beaucoup pour le dîner. C'était très bon et très agréable. J'ai aimé le gâteau au chocolat. Tu es très gentille.
À bientôt,
Nora

exercises.question: What is Nora thanking Marie for?
Which phrase means 'Thank you very much'?
Merci beaucoup *** le dîner.
C'était très ***.
Which sentence is appropriate in a thank-you note?

lessons.title: Writing an Invitation
lessons.description: Learn how to write a simple invitation to a birthday party, dinner, or small event.

grammar.title: Basic Invitation Format
grammar.text: A simple invitation should include the event, the date, the time, and the place. Use 'Je t'invite...' for a friend. Use 'chez moi' to say 'at my place'. You can finish with 'Réponds-moi' or 'J'espère te voir'.

lessons.reading:
Salut Karim,
Je t'invite à mon anniversaire samedi à 18h chez moi. Il y a de la musique, des gâteaux et des amis. Viens avec ta sœur si tu veux. Réponds-moi vite !
À bientôt,
Lina

exercises.question: What event is Lina inviting Karim to?
When is the event?

samedi à 18h chez ***.
Which information should an invitation include?
